html:
The Knights Hospitaller, a Catholic military order, ruled Malta from 1530 to 1798 and were known from then on as the Knights of Malta.

The order had begun in Jerusalem in the age of the Crusades and ruled Rhodes until the Ottomans drove it out in 1522. The emperor Charles V granted it Malta, for the yearly rent of a falcon. The knights, younger sons of noble families from across Catholic Europe, made Malta a fortress against the Ottomans and the corsairs of North Africa.

They held off the Great Siege of 1565, built Valletta, and ran a hospital famous across Europe. Their galleys raided Muslim shipping and brought slaves to the island. Napoleon ended their rule in 1798. The order still exists, based in Rome, as a charity.
sum: The Knights Hospitaller, a Catholic military order, ruled Malta from 1530 to 1798 and were known from then on as the Knights of Malta.
